Reading the file set_ftrace_filter does three things.
1) shows whether or not filters are set for the function tracer
2) shows what functions are set for the function tracer
3) shows what triggers are set on any functions
3 is independent from 1 and 2.
The way this file currently works is that it is a state machine
and as you read it
column2: it may change state. But this assumption breaks

column1: when you use lseek() on the file. The state machine gets out of sync
and the t_show() may use the wrong pointer and cause a kernel oops.
Luckily
column2: this will only kill the app that does the lseek

column1: dies while holding a mutex. This prevents anyone else from using the
set_ftrace_filter file (or any other function tracing file for that matter).
A real fix for this is to rewrite the code
column2: but that is too much for

column1: a -rc release or stable. This patch simply disables llseek on the
set_ftrace_filter() file for now
column2: and we can do the proper fix for the

column1: next major release.
